chat.text: Mmmmm....cake...

chat.text: aint nobody don't like no parfait

chat.text: :birthday:

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: I think "p=reject" is just a horrible thing to have called it in DMARC, but that's a lot of milk under the bridge and now we are laying in it.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: layering*

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Everyone with cameras on has substantial beards going on.  I feel inferior.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Beardless chairs.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Join us!

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: +1 Bron!

chat.author: Brian Godiksen
chat.text: You just sign twice?

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: This is the ESP case, first sign for the client, then for the ESP

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: you set From: resnick@pete.com at the point that you sign as pete.com -- either first, or with a change

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: that's the ND thingy for ESPs

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: For clarity, I absolutely think the rule SHOULD be Option 1 (modulo: not be treated as valid dkim2) -- but the rule that makes it so should be in the BCP doc

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: Do BCPs have rules, or just suggestions and recommendations?

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: because -spec tells you how the mechanism works, and the BCP tells you what to do with it

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: yes, dkim2-spec say's it invalid dkim2 and dkim2-bcp say's you should reject invalid dkim2

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: Somewhere in between

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: not invalid dkim2, non-authentic dkim2

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Todd: I would say they have rules that discuss proper use, but do not alter the standard(s) they discuss.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: At worst, you can say someone's practices do not conform to the BCP, not that someone is violating the protocol.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: yes, and I think this belongs in that.  People can choose not to do it but they risk being blocked later.  The mechanism works fine for bounces etc regardless

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: Pete will Re-Pete

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: Order always matters, this is not special

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: I=1 must be authentic, I=N can either keep an existing authentic value, or create a new authentic value which then must be authentic to "d=" at hop N

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: +1 to Tobias - very good description

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text:
The rules are pretty simple:
1) If a DKIM2-Signature introduces a new 5322.From, its signing domain must be aligned
2) The top-most DKIM2-Signature's signing domain must be aligned with 5321.mail-from

chat.author: Trent Adams
chat.text: Yup

chat.author: Faisal Misle
chat.text: all good

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: [meta] "must confirm consensus on the list" is a great circuit-breaker against infinite discussion!

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Always in the chair toolbox.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: replay is 1000% harder because you need to be able to sign as a participant in the original mailflow.  But that's a real risk if you can get a message sent to a domain you control from the domain you want to attack, you can then replace it with an honest recipe and and authentic "From" rewrite and send the message on, having changed absolutely everything to be a brand new message!

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: Validating against d= domain using relaxed procedures conflicts with the proposed spec change requiring that the d= domain exactly match the From domain, doesn't it?

chat.author: Trent Adams
chat.text: Apologies, as I have to leave to pick my daughter up from school... so I'll just leave this here... my comment on Wei's topic is that we should steer clear of talking about DMARC at this point, and allow the DKIM2 work evolve naturally to (potentially) take on similar alignment features (but not force the issue now).

chat.author: Richard Clayton
chat.text: Wei's scheme is sort of taken over by earlier events today ... BUT people will still need to concentrate on the different ways in which a domain can be matched (in DKIM2 and DMARC)

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: Don't think we should do DKIM2->DKIM->DKIM2, it'll be a wart that never goes away

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: The existence of the auth= tag will discourage adoption of DKIM2, in my opinion. Why bother ever adding auth=dkim2 to my DMARC policy record if I can just skate with dkim/spf?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Sorry, all: Which was the thing to be inserted in the agenda before PQC?  My self-note got overwritten.

chat.author: Jennifer Lantz
chat.text: My concern is that dmarc is usually at the top and if they are using multiple systems not all will have dkim2 so it might be hard to include dkim2 for a long time

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: @**Todd Because more of your legit mail will pass?

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Charsets was before PQC

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Thank you

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: @Murray Kucherawy the non-UTF-8 text stuff

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: datatracker agenda updated so we don't lose it; agenda on the slides has not been updated

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: I think I agree with Bron. There's value in having the rt= populated. If the sender is going to do the lookup and declare it in the DKIM2-Signature, putting it in another tag would be better than dropping rt=.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: <without hats> +1 Bron and Allen

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: I'm with Bron on this aswell

chat.author: David Conradie
chat.text: Yep - receiver is doing work anyway and should continue to do so. Don’t make the sender look ahead

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: But all of this assumes system B doesn't modify at all. If it does, nothing in the signature matters because it can't be authenticated.

chat.author: Alex Brotman
chat.text: With the auth= tag, should we expect that when the same 5322.From (whether direct or by treewalk) is leveraged by a sender, but from multiple sending infrastructures (which may not all support DKIM2), the auth= tag just lists all three mechanisms ?

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: How is Domain B defined for the purposes of a DMARC lookup in this scenario?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: As chair: I agree, don't cross post.

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: DMARC is currently keyed to RFC5322.From

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: @Todd yeah, that's another reason why rt= has value, because B the domain of the rt=

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: But I'm asking in the lookback scenario where C is doing the work to look up B's DMARC record, what domain is used to define B's DMARC policy?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Aw, crap. Todd is right.

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: "v=spf1 ?all"

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: that would only happen in the from munging case

chat.author: Alex Brotman
chat.text: Did notes stop getting updated, or just nothing to put in them?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: People failed to keep typing.

chat.author: Alex Brotman
chat.text: I thought it was just broken for me, apologies

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Claude, finish the meeting notes.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: We're conflating "DMARC policy" and "I support dkim2".  The thing I want to be able to look up is "domain X claims to support dkim2" - because if messages sent to it break the chain at that point, then you know they're a replay

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text: sure, that makes sense, but how do you determine what "domain X" is when you're looking at the previous hop?

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: rt=foo@DOMAINX

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: on the topmost DKIM2-Signature

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Wei's seems like a good plan.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: that's the domain where it left the DKIM2 ecosystem.  Any further domains are potential replay

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: but this only works of dkim2 is still valid

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: if not everything is essentially free-text

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: @Tobias no.  In the "DOMAINX" supports DKIM2 then either it's invalid DKIM2 or valid DKIM2, and either way it's a replay

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: because if DOMAINX really handled it, then it will have had another DKIM2-Signature on top

chat.author: Tobias Herkula
chat.text: i meant it the way, if dkim2 is invalid i will not even invest in lookingup any policies

chat.author: Todd Herr
chat.text:
relying on rt= will require some unknown (maybe small) percentage of domains to publish DMARC records when they've never done so before.
I don't say that as a criticism, but it's certainly possible

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: @Tobias if it's missing in the interim stage, then it's a mailing list which didn't support DKIM2 or whatevers

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: @Todd yes, that's the downside

chat.text: but then i will handle it the "old" way
